Package io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.nt

Class Nt4Server

java.lang.Object
io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.nt.Nt4Server
public final class Nt4Server extends Object
A NetworkTables 4 server, so AdvantageScope can connect to a robot the way it connects to an FRC robot: ws://<robot>:5810.

Written in plain Java 8 with no libraries, to run on a REV Control Hub. The robot's code sets values with set(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.Object), which stores them and returns at once; each client has its own thread that sends them, so a slow or lost connection never holds up the robot's loop.

FTC rule R704 forbids third-party telemetry over Wi-Fi at competitions. Start a server only for practice.

Covered: the plain HTTP request AdvantageScope sends before connecting, the 4.1, 4.0 and rtt subprotocols, publish, unpublish, setproperties, subscribe with prefix, topicsonly and periodic, and unsubscribe. Not covered: the all option (each send carries the latest value), meta-topics such as $clients, saving persistent topics, TLS and NetworkTables 3.

    • set

      public void set(String name, String type, Object value)
      Sets a topic's value, creating the topic the first time. type is an NT4 type string: boolean, double, int, float, string, raw, double[] and the other arrays, struct:Pose2d, structschema, and so on. The value is a Boolean, Double, Long, Float, String, byte[], boolean[], double[], long[], float[] or String[] to match. A topic's type is fixed by its first value; a value of another type is ignored. A value equal to the last is not sent again.
